beats.note: Medical News Today traces the idea to theories from 1947 and the 1970s, neither of which is now backed by the data.

beats.context: A 1995 JAMA review pooled 23 blinded, placebo controlled studies from 16 reports. Sugar did not affect behaviour or cognitive performance.

beats.text: A small effect was not ruled out.
beats.note: The authors wrote that a small effect, or effects on subsets of children, could not be ruled out.
In a 1994 study, 35 boys aged 5 to 7 all received aspartame. Mothers told it was sugar rated their sons as significantly more hyperactive.
Those mothers maintained more physical closeness, and showed trends to criticise and talk to their sons, according to Medical News Today.
Medical News Today says the jury is still out for children with ADHD.

beats.text: The sugar was not the variable.
